verses.1: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the vision that first appeared to me.
verses.2: I saw the vision while I was in Susa, the capital in the province of Elam. I saw the vision as I stood on the Ulai Canal.
verses.3: I raised my eyes and saw, and there stood a ram before the canal. It had two horns, and both horns were tall. One was taller than the other, and the taller one grew stronger over time.
verses.4: I watched the ram charge in all directions—toward the west, the north, and the south. No beast could stand before it, and no one could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
verses.5: As I was watching, a goat with a single horn came from the west, crossing the whole earth without touching the ground. The goat had a horn between its eyes.
verses.6: It came up to the two-horned ram I had seen standing before the canal. It ran toward the ram with the strength of its rage.
verses.7: I watched the goat attack the ram, rushing at it with fury. It struck the ram and broke both its horns. There was no strength in the ram to stand before it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled it, and no one could rescue the ram from its power.
verses.8: The goat became very strong, and when its power reached its height, the great horn was broken. In its place, four horns sprang up toward the four winds of the heavens.
verses.9: From one of these horns came another small horn, which grew even stronger, extending toward the south, the east, and the land of the sacred.
verses.10: It grew so strong that it reached the host of heaven, and it cast some of the host and some of the stars to the ground, trampling them.
verses.11: It grew up to the leader of the host, and it removed the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation.
verses.12: The host was given over to the small horn through rebellion. It cast truth to the ground and acted and succeeded.
verses.13: I heard a holy one speaking, saying to another holy one, "How long will the vision last—the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the trampling of the sanctuary and the host?"
verses.14: He said to me, "For two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings, then the sanctuary will be cleansed."
verses.15: As I, Daniel, was looking at the vision, I was trying to understand it, when suddenly a figure like a human stood before me.
verses.16: I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, and it called out, saying, "Gabriel, make this man understand the vision."
verses.17: He came up to where I was standing. When he came near, I was startled and fell on my face, and he said to me, "Son of man, the vision is for the end of time."
verses.18: While he was speaking with me, I fell on my face on the ground, and he touched me and helped me to my feet.
verses.19: He said, "I will tell you what will happen in the end of days, for the vision is for the end of time."
verses.20: The ram you saw with the two horns represents the kings of Media and Persia.
verses.21: The goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
verses.22: The broken horn and the four that rose in its place represent four kingdoms from the same people, which will arise not by their own strength.
verses.23: At the end of their kingdoms, when the time of lawlessness is complete, a king with a bold face and great understanding will rise.
verses.24: His strength will be strong, but not through his own strength. He will do wonders and deceive many. He will grow powerful, strike down the mighty, and the holy people.
verses.25: Through deceit, he will succeed. In his heart he will grow great, and he will destroy many through deception. He will stand against the leader of leaders, but he will be crushed.
verses.26: The vision of the evening and morning, which was told truthfully, is for many days to come. You, Daniel, must seal the vision until the time of the end.
verses.27: I, Daniel, was troubled and sick, and I rose to do the king's work, but I was stunned by the vision and no one could understand it.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "abomination of desolation" renders the Hebrew as a fixed phrase, reflecting the theological context without altering the wording.
- v. 25: "deceit" is used to capture the meaning of the Hebrew root for "deceitful" (שָׁקַר), which also appears in the phrase "deceitful in heart" (לֵב־שֹׁקֵר).
- v. 26: "seal the vision" reflects the imperative to keep the meaning hidden until the time of fulfillment, as the Hebrew uses the word for "seal" (סָתַם) in a prophetic context.

[3] I raised my eyes and saw, and there stood a ram before the canal. It had two horns, and both horns were tall. One was taller than the other, and the taller one grew stronger over time.
[4] I watched the ram charge in all directions—toward the west, the north, and the south. No beast could stand before it, and no one could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
[5] As I was watching, a goat with a single horn came from the west, crossing the whole earth without touching the ground. The goat had a horn between its eyes.
[6] It came up to the two-horned ram I had seen standing before the canal. It ran toward the ram with the strength of its rage.

[9] From one of these horns came another small horn, which grew even stronger, extending toward the south, the east, and the land of the sacred.
[10] It grew so strong that it reached the host of heaven, and it cast some of the host and some of the stars to the ground, trampling them.
[11] It grew up to the leader of the host, and it removed the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation.

[13] I heard a holy one speaking, saying to another holy one, "How long will the vision last—the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the trampling of the sanctuary and the host?"
[14] He said to me, "For two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings, then the sanctuary will be cleansed."
[15] As I, Daniel, was looking at the vision, I was trying to understand it, when suddenly a figure like a human stood before me.
[16] I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, and it called out, saying, "Gabriel, make this man understand the vision."
[17] He came up to where I was standing. When he came near, I was startled and fell on my face, and he said to me, "Son of man, the vision is for the end of time."

[21] The goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.

[25] Through deceit, he will succeed. In his heart he will grow great, and he will destroy many through deception. He will stand against the leader of leaders, but he will be crushed.

[27] I, Daniel, was troubled and sick, and I rose to do the king's work, but I was stunned by the vision and no one could understand it.
